haiku-low.q1: It still lands in the same account, because matching is by Google sub, and email is checked only when the sub is not linked. Users.email never changes.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the existing account's password at Confirm your password (POST /auth/google/confirm). A correct bcrypt check inserts user_identities, then the session starts.
haiku-low.q3: The 5th wrong password locks the account for 15 minutes, resets the counter, and deletes the pending link and cookie. The user must restart Google sign-in after the lock.
haiku-low.q4: No email match: a users row is created with password_hash NULL and email_verified_at set, plus a user_identities row, then a session starts. Unverified email: redirect to /login saying to use email and password.
haiku-low.q5: Error page: sign-in expired or invalid, try again. The attempt record was already removed by GETDEL or expired after 10 minutes, so nothing is written and no session is created.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row and a new sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days). The old sessions row for any existing sid is deleted first. Then redirect to next or /home.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required; the session user must equal the attempt user_id. If the sub is linked to another user, Settings shows it is linked to another account and nothing is written.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis under oidc:attempt:STATE with a 10 minute TTL. The callback removes it with an atomic GETDEL as its first step; an unused one expires.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis under oidc:pending:ID, holding user_id, google_sub, google_email and next. The browser holds only the random ID in an HttpOnly, Secure pending_link cookie. Deleted on link success or lockout, otherwise it expires after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: In the PostgreSQL user_identities table. UNIQUE(provider, subject) allows one user per Google account, and UNIQUE(user_id, provider) allows one Google account per user.
haiku-low.q11: The user is redirected to /login with Google sign-in failed, try again. The exchange is not retried, because the code is single-use and the attempt record is gone; the user must start again.
haiku-low.q12: The attempt record's mode field (login or link) tells it apart. For link mode, the session user must equal the attempt's user_id, otherwise the user gets the expired or invalid error page.

sonnet.q1: Matching is by sub only, so the linked sub is found in user_identities and they land in the same account with a new session (start_session). The changed Gmail address does not matter, and Google never changes users.email.
sonnet.q2: The user is shown 'Confirm your password' (pending record oidc:pending:ID in Redis, TTL 10 min, with pending_link cookie). They must POST the correct password to /auth/google/confirm (bcrypt check, not locked, pending record still exists). Then failed_logins is reset to 0, a user_identities row is inserted, the pending record is deleted and the cookie cleared, and start_session runs.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password increments failed_logins and shows the form again. On the 5th wrong password locked_until is set to now + 15 min, the counter is reset, the pending record is deleted and the cookie cleared, and 'Account temporarily locked' is shown. The user must start Google sign-in again after the lock.
sonnet.q4: If email_verified is true and no users row matches the lowercased email, one transaction creates a new user (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) plus a user_identities row, then a session starts. If email_verified is false, the user is redirected to /login with a message to use email and password; nothing is written.
sonnet.q5: Both cases give the same result. The oidc:attempt record has a 10 min TTL, so it is expired after 12 min, and a second load finds it already consumed by GETDEL. Either way GETDEL finds no record and the user sees the error page 'sign-in expired or invalid, try again'. Nothing is written.
sonnet.q6: It creates a new sessions row and sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days, slid forward on use) via start_session(user_id). The sessions row for any sid the browser already had is deleted first. Then it redirects to next if that is a relative path on the site, otherwise to /home.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email match is required, and the emails may differ. The session user must equal the attempt's user_id, otherwise it goes to the error page. If the sub is already linked to another user, the user is sent to Settings with 'this Google account is linked to another account' and nothing is inserted. If already linked to this user, Settings shows 'already linked'.
sonnet.q8: They are kept in the Redis record oidc:attempt:<state> (TTL 10 min), written by the start step. It holds mode, user_id (link mode), nonce, code_verifier and next. The callback deletes it with an atomic GETDEL as its first step. If it is never used, it expires after the TTL.
sonnet.q9: It is held in Redis as oidc:pending:<id> (TTL 10 min), holding user_id, google_sub, google_email and next. The browser holds only the random <id> in an HttpOnly, Secure pending_link cookie. It is deleted when the link succeeds or the account locks, and otherwise expires.
sonnet.q10: It is stored in the new PostgreSQL table user_identities (user_id, provider='google', subject = Google sub, email_at_link, linked_at). UNIQUE(provider, subject) means a Google account links to only one user. UNIQUE(user_id, provider) means a user has only one Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user is redirected to /login with 'Google sign-in failed, try again'. The exchange is not retried, because the code is single-use and the attempt record is already gone. The user starts again from the button. Nothing is written.
sonnet.q12: The attempt record's mode field (login or link) set by the start step, read via GETDEL in the callback. For link mode the attempt stores user_id, and the callback checks that the current session user equals that attempt user_id. If not, it shows the error page and links nothing.
